back: The surplus per unit of land after production and transport costs: price − production cost − transport cost.
The distance from the market at which economic rent falls to zero, so the crop is no longer worth growing.

front: Economic rent for a crop at distance d
back: Rent = price − production cost − (transport rate × d). Transport rate is cost per tonne per kilometre.
Five regions, I to V: rainfall falls and becomes less reliable from I (over 1 000 mm) to V (below about 450 mm).
Tea, coffee, fruit, forestry and dairy in the cool, wet Eastern Highlands.
Extensive ranching and wildlife; crops such as sugarcane and citrus only with irrigation.
Isolated state, one market town, flat uniform plain, profit-maximising farmers, transport cost proportional to distance, no government.
Market gardening and dairying, forestry, arable crops, livestock ranching, then wilderness, in rings around the market.
Real land is not uniform; transport, refrigeration, irrigation and policy alter the rings, and there are many markets.
